missing_spec_content.spec_text: investigate the effectiveness of different materials as thermal insulators and the factors that may affect the thermal insulation properties of a material.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson only covers the first half of the practical: comparing different materials (keyPoints[3].content: "The independent variable is the material"). It never covers investigating the factors that affect a material's insulating properties, such as thickness or number of layers. Instead, thickness appears only as a control variable ("Control variables include ... the thickness of material").

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Investigate thermal conductivity using rods of different materials.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson does not mention any activity that compares thermal conductivity using rods of different materials. This is listed as a skills opportunity rather than core content, so it may be lower priority.

factual_errors.text: streamlining reduces air resistance, so less kinetic energy is wasted pushing through the air
factual_errors.correction: For a vehicle moving at steady speed, the kinetic store does not decrease. The energy transferred doing work against air resistance comes from the fuel's chemical store, and streamlining reduces that wasted transfer. The same wording appears in keyPoints[1].writeBullets[4], keyPoints[3].content, keyPoints[3].keyTerms[2].def and revisionCardBullets[11]. This is a minor imprecision.

factual_errors.text: A contact force between surfaces that converts kinetic energy to thermal energy
factual_errors.correction: A force does not itself convert energy. Work done against friction transfers energy from the kinetic store to the thermal store of the surfaces and surroundings. This is a minor imprecision.

wrong_terms.text: Using oil or similar material between surfaces to reduce friction and heat loss
wrong_terms.spec_term: unwanted energy transfers / dissipated (spec: "ways of reducing unwanted energy transfers, for example through lubrication"). The lesson itself says 'lost' is not to be used (introTips[2]).

wrong_terms.text: Shaping an object to reduce air resistance and the kinetic energy lost to drag
wrong_terms.spec_term: dissipated / 'wasted' (spec: "energy is dissipated, so that it is stored in less useful ways. This energy is often described as being 'wasted'")

wrong_terms.text: This reduces heat loss through the roof by conduction and convection
wrong_terms.spec_term: rate of energy transfer / unwanted energy transfers (the same 'heat loss' wording appears in revisionCardBullets[8]: "slows heat loss to the surroundings")

transferred / stored (spec: "Energy can be transferred usefully, stored or dissipated"). The lesson elsewhere uses a forms model, e.g. keyPoints[1].content "useful light energy", and keyPoints[0].content "The total mechanical energy falls".
